characters.description: A member of Willard's organization who brings a selection of vetted magical weapons for Amber. His delivery lets her choose a sword suited to defending herself from supernatural opponents while Val prepares for a dangerous mission.
characters.name: Corporal Clark

characters.description: The hungry son of a slain troll whom Val finds scavenging near the coffee shop. She buys him food and offers him limited paid cleaning work after learning that the trolls around him make him compete for meals.
characters.name: Orphaned troll boy

characters.description: Val gives her the recovered journal and financial help from the dragon mission. She considers moving closer to Val and Amber.
characters.name: Val's mother

recaps.ending: Ty and Dr. Walker open every life cell and administer Zoltan's cure to the imprisoned Stormforge dragons, including Zav's uncle. Val kills the silver-dragon leader, while Zav and his sister defeat the other immediate conspirators. The Stormforge queen arrives with reinforcements, accepts Val as Zav's mate, and takes her badly wounded son home to recover. One week later, all the prisoners are free and treated, although some face a long recovery. Zav returns healed, and his clan again controls a majority of the ruling council and Dragon Justice Court. He repairs Val's mold-damaged house, and the two begin dating openly. Val, Dimitri, Nin, and Zoltan name their thriving coffee shop The Sable Dragon. Inga joins its support network and cares for the orphaned troll boy. Questions about Val's elven family, possible dragon retaliation, and older enemies remain open, while a new killing near Tulalip Resort Casino points to Val's next investigation.
recaps.in_short: When Nin's long-missing grandfather Ty arrives gravely ill, Val and her allies cure him and learn that Silverclaw dragons are secretly holding infected Stormforge dragons in the Crying Caverns. Zoltan develops a cure, Zav tests it on himself, and the group mounts a covert rescue. Zav fakes his capture while Val, Ty, Dr. Walker, and Sindari infiltrate the prison. The apparent betrayal by Zav's sister proves to be part of his plan. Val kills the silver-dragon leader, the conspirators are defeated, and Stormforge reinforcements secure the caverns. Every captive is freed and treated, including Zav's uncle. Zav survives serious wounds, his mother accepts Val as his mate, and the Stormforges regain political control. Zav returns to repair Val's home and begin openly dating her. The coffee shop becomes The Sable Dragon, while a new local killing sets up the next case.

recaps.text: Previously: Val Thorvald is a half-elf investigator who handles dangers involving the magical community while raising her daughter, Amber. Zav, a Stormforge dragon, has claimed Val as his mate, though their bond remains complicated by dragon customs and her determination to choose her own path. Sindari, a summoned magical tiger, fights beside her. Willard directs Val's work, while Dimitri, Nin, and the vampire alchemist Zoltan share her growing household and business network. Val and her partners are establishing a coffee shop for magical clientele. Her elven heritage has also brought new family connections and unresolved questions. Threats carried forward include anti-dragon rebels, a leak connected to the elven court, and an escaped scientist.

So far this book: A wounded older gnome collapses in Val's yard and is identified as Ty, Nin's grandfather, who vanished twenty years ago. Orcs attack while trying to recover him, but Val, Willard, and Sindari drive them off. Ty is suffering from an unusual bacterial infection, and Zoltan begins creating a treatment that requires a rare plant from a former elven sanctuary. Meanwhile, Zav reports that his missing uncle has weakened his mother's political position. His mother wants him to abandon his bond with Val and accept a politically useful dragon mate. The proposed mate follows him to Earth, restrains Val, and challenges Zav. He defeats her, refuses the alliance, and affirms that Val is his chosen mate, but the rival remains nearby. Val continues the urgent search for Ty's medicine with help from Zav and her elven half-sister.

So far this book: Val's group obtains the plant Zoltan needs and sends it back for Ty's treatment. At the abandoned elven homes, Val and her half-sister find letters and a journal showing that Val's parents shared a sustained and loving relationship, though the reason her father left is still unknown. The rival female dragon finds them, tries to compel Val to reject Zav, and sets the dwelling and nearby trees on fire when Val resists. Val's half-sister protects them and helps extinguish the blaze. Back home, Zav reports that Ty has stabilized. Val and Zav commit to treating each other as mates despite his family's demands and the rival's threats. Their private moment is interrupted when Nin announces that Ty has awakened, leaving him ready to explain his disappearance and why his pursuers want him back.

So far this book: Ty reveals that Silverclaw allies operate a hidden prison in the Crying Caverns on the gnomish world. More than twenty weakened Stormforge dragons are held there in life cells and kept unconscious by an engineered infection. Ty was abducted to maintain the prison, escaped after Zav's uncle was brought in, and came to Val because a dwarf believed she and Chopper could help. A Silverclaw dragon follows Ty to Earth and attacks Val with orc reinforcements, but Val, Sindari, and Zav repel them. Zav confirms that Ty believes his account. An open Stormforge response could prompt the captors to kill the prisoners and start a war, so the group considers a covert rescue. Because Zoltan's cure has only worked on Ty, Zav agrees to be deliberately infected and treated to prove that it can save dragons.

So far this book: Val prepares for a mission she may not survive, strengthens Amber's training, and helps a hungry troll child by arranging food and paid work at the shop. Willard recruits Dr. Walker as armed medical support. Zoltan proves that his cure works on Zav and discovers the same infection in barbecue delivered to the house. Zav decides to infect himself again and pretend to be incapacitated so the enemy will carry him into the prison. Val finally tells him about her asthma, and he accepts her vulnerability without questioning her ability to fight. After acknowledging their love, they begin the operation. Val, Ty, and Dr. Walker portal to the gnomish world and see Zav taken into the Crying Caverns with several dragons, including his sister. Her apparent cooperation suggests betrayal, but Val's team continues into the trapped complex because Zav and the prisoners still need help.

So far this book: Val, Ty, Dr. Walker, and Sindari fight through the cavern entrance. Val then separates from the others to draw the searching dragons away while Ty and the doctor seek the life cells with Zoltan's cure. Captured and brought to Zav, Val overhears a plan to kill the queen and seize the Dragon Justice Court and ruling council. Her charms and mental training keep the conspirators from reading her thoughts. Zav's sister appears to stop Val from helping him, but the betrayal is a ruse arranged with Zav. He is only feigning unconsciousness. When a trap disrupts the chamber, Zav and his sister attack the hostile dragons. Val kills the silver-dragon leader with Chopper, and the other immediate conspirators are defeated. The group reaches the prison chamber, where dozens of infected dragons remain sealed in life cells. Zav stays behind to delay approaching enemies while his sister goes to summon their family.

By the end: Ty and Dr. Walker open the life cells and inject the freed dragons with Zoltan's cure. Zav's uncle awakens, but an opposing dragon attacks before he can recover. The Stormforge queen arrives with reinforcements, kills the intruder, and sends help to Zav. Val later finds Zav seriously wounded. His mother accepts Val as his mate and takes him home for healing. A week later, every captive has been freed and treated, though some recoveries may take months. The Stormforges regain majority control of the dragon ruling council and Dragon Justice Court. Zav returns fully healed, removes the mold from Val's house, and magically restores its damaged second floor. He and Val plan a formal date and continue their relationship by mutual choice. Val gives her mother the recovered journal and money from the mission. The coffee shop thrives under the name The Sable Dragon, with Inga joining its security effort and caring for the orphaned troll boy. Willard also reports a new killing near Tulalip Resort Casino.

characters.description: The only openly practicing professional wizard in Chicago, Harry Dresden works as a private investigator and an occasional paid consultant for the police, taking the cases ordinary detectives cannot explain. Orphaned young and raised by a manipulative sorcerer he was forced to kill in self-defense as a teenager, he lives under the wary eye of the White Council, the governing body of wizards, which once nearly executed him for that killing and still watches him for any sign he might turn magic to murder. Wry, stubborn, and chronically broke, he lives alone with his cat and a talking spirit, keeps an old-fashioned chivalric streak, and refuses to walk away from trouble he could safely leave alone.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The head of the Chicago Police Department's Special Investigations unit, the division handed every case too strange for anyone else to touch. Small, blond, and easy to underestimate, she is a relentless and honest cop who calls in Harry Dresden as a consultant when the evidence stops making ordinary sense. She does not fully grasp the magical world she keeps brushing against and distrusts what she cannot verify, which puts recurring strain on their partnership, but her courage and her refusal to look away from ugly truths are never in question.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A spirit of air and intellect bound into a bleached human skull that Harry keeps in his basement laboratory. Bob is a centuries-old store of magical knowledge, especially the practical mechanics of spells and potions, and serves as Harry's irreverent research assistant and sounding board. Amoral by nature and endlessly interested in appetites and gossip, he helps or needles Harry by turns, and his memory of older magic than the modern Council practices makes him one of Harry's most valuable and least trustworthy resources.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A Warden of the White Council, one of the wizard-enforcers who hunt down practitioners who break the Laws of Magic. Grim, humorless, and convinced of Harry's guilt, Morgan was assigned to watch Harry after the killing that first brought him before the Council, and he waits for any excuse to see the old sentence carried out. When people begin dying by forbidden magic in Chicago, he warns Harry that a single misstep will cost him his head, and shadows the investigation as much to trap Harry as to solve it.
characters.name: Donald Morgan

characters.description: A sharp, ambitious reporter for a tabloid covering the strange and the supernatural, and the woman Harry is seeing. Susan is drawn to Harry as much for the real magic he represents as for himself, and she keeps pressing him for the story he will not give her. Fearless to the point of recklessness, she inserts herself into his investigation despite the danger, unwilling to be protected or left behind.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: The most powerful crime lord in Chicago, a soft-spoken, coldly intelligent man who has quietly unified the city's underworld. One of the murder victims was his employee, and Marcone takes an interest in Harry's investigation, by turns offering him money to stand down and warning him off. He operates by his own rigid code and prefers order to chaos, which makes him a pragmatic and genuinely dangerous figure who cannot be bought and will not be bullied.
characters.name: John Marcone

characters.description: A Red Court vampire who runs an upscale brothel, the Velvet Room, in Chicago. Beautiful and composed in the human seeming she wears, she is a creature of appetite and pride beneath it. One of her women was among the murdered, and Harry's questions provoke her; a clash between them leaves her humiliated and nursing a grudge that will outlast this case. She is a reminder that the vampire courts watch the city closely.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A tiny dewdrop faerie of the wilds whom Harry catches and bargains with for information. Vain, greedy for pizza and shiny things, and prone to grand self-importance despite his size, Toot-toot scouts places Harry cannot reach and reports back in exchange for tribute. The arrangement is Harry's first small, working relationship with the faerie folk.
characters.name: Toot-Toot

characters.description: The dark sorcerer behind the heart-ripping murders. A failed, resentful man who discovered real magical talent late and gave himself over to it without restraint, Victor built his power around a new drug that grants users a burst of the Sight, and he kills with a brutal ritual that tears the hearts from his victims at a distance, drawing on the energy of storms to fuel it. Working from a lake house outside the city, he treats magic purely as a weapon and a path to wealth, and turns it on Harry the moment Harry gets close.
characters.name: Victor Sells

recaps.ending: Victor Sells is dead, killed by his own storm-drawn power when Harry turned the ritual back on him, and the heart-ripping murders stop. Susan Rodriguez, who had secretly taken the Sight-granting drug to follow the story, survives the ordeal, and her relationship with Harry deepens even as the danger of his world becomes undeniable to her. Murphy, after briefly arresting Harry when she found him at the scene, accepts that he was working to stop the killer, and the partnership between Special Investigations and Chicago's wizard holds. The White Council lifts its immediate threat, though Warden Morgan remains convinced Harry is dangerous and keeps watching. Harry also leaves two lasting marks on his future: the vampire Bianca now hates him and will nurse the grudge, and the crime lord Gentleman Johnny Marcone has taken his measure and filed him away as a man worth watching. Broke and battered as ever, Harry returns to his small practice, his cat, and Bob the skull, a little more established as the city's reluctant supernatural defender.
recaps.in_short: Harry Dresden, the only wizard in Chicago's phone book, is hired from two directions at once: his police-consultant work brings him a double murder committed by heart-ripping black magic, and a worried wife hires him to find her missing husband, Victor. Because only forbidden magic could have killed that way, Warden Morgan of the White Council threatens Harry with execution if another such death occurs and treats him as the suspect. Investigating, Harry ties the murders to a new drug that grants the Sight and to the vampire Bianca, clashes with crime lord Johnny Marcone, and discovers that the missing husband, Victor Sells, has become a dark sorcerer killing at a distance with storm-powered rituals. Victor turns demons and conjurations on Harry. In a final confrontation at Victor's lake house during a storm, Harry, aided by the reporter Susan Rodriguez, destroys Victor and his ritual, clears himself with the Council, and keeps Murphy's uneasy trust.

recaps.text: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard, takes on two problems at once. Karrin Murphy of the police department's Special Investigations unit brings him to a grisly double murder: a mob bodyguard and a call girl killed in bed by magic that tore the hearts from their chests, a spell of terrible power and skill. That same morning a nervous woman named Monica hires Harry to find her missing husband, Victor. Harry recognizes that only forbidden black magic could have committed the killings, which puts him in immediate danger from his own kind: the White Council forbids using magic to kill, and Harry already lives under a suspended death sentence for a killing in his past. He begins pulling at both cases, not yet aware that they are the same case.

Warden Morgan of the White Council shadows Harry, promising to see him executed the instant another magical death occurs and treating Harry himself as the prime suspect. Harry's inquiries link the murders to a new street drug that grants a brief flash of magical Sight, and to the world of the vampire courts: he confronts Bianca, a Red Court vampire who runs a brothel and employed the dead woman, and the meeting ends in mutual injury and lasting enmity. Meanwhile the missing husband, Victor Sells, proves far harder to find than a runaway should be. Harry's digging draws the attention of Gentleman Johnny Marcone, Chicago's crime lord, whose own man was one of the victims; Marcone tries to buy Harry off the case, then to warn him away, and is refused.

The killer strikes again, and the spell is turned on Harry himself; only luck and quick warding save him, and Morgan's threat becomes immediate. Harry realizes the murders, the drug, and the missing man all trace back to Victor Sells, who has become a self-taught dark sorcerer working from a lake house outside the city and killing with a storm-fueled ritual that rips out hearts at a distance. Victor sends a demon and other conjured horrors after Harry to stop the investigation. Battered, hunted by his own Council, and distrusted by Murphy after he is caught withholding information, Harry races to reach Victor before the next storm gives the sorcerer the power to kill again - and before the next heart torn out is his own.

Harry and Susan drive out to the lake house as a storm gathers, where Victor is preparing a mass ritual. Susan, having secretly taken the Sight-granting drug, is overwhelmed and endangered, and Harry faces Victor amid conjured scorpions and demons with almost nothing left. Turning Victor's own storm-drawn power against him, Harry destroys the sorcerer and his ritual, ending the killings. Murphy, arriving to find the aftermath, arrests Harry briefly but comes to accept he was on her side, and their working partnership survives. The Council's death sentence is lifted for now. Harry is left exhausted, cleared, and more entangled than ever in the hidden world, having made a lasting enemy of Bianca and drawn the lasting interest of Marcone.

characters.description: A Legion Varus centurion, Galina Turov's subordinate and lover, and Etta's father. He is maintaining a false explanation for his daughter's move to Dust World while privately trying to contain the consequences of her dealings with Claver.
characters.name: James McGill

characters.description: The tribune commanding Legion Varus and McGill's superior officer and lover. At his family home, she supports the public claim that Etta went to Dust World for protection.
characters.name: Galina Turov

characters.description: McGill's underage daughter, now living on Dust World. Her family has been told that she left for safety, while McGill conceals the real circumstances of her departure and her involvement in a transaction with Claver.
characters.name: Etta

characters.description: A concealed adversary who appears near McGill's home after Etta's transaction and creates an immediate threat there.
characters.name: Claver

characters.description: The leading body in a clone network that also uses physically powerful Class Three workers. The workers remain loyal to this primary line and identify McGill by the equipment taken from its Earth body.
characters.name: Claver Prime

characters.description: The leader of the Dust World colony and operator of its clandestine revival system. He restores McGill with an illegal process that combines stored DNA and tapper memories, then requires him to keep the operation secret.
characters.name: Etta's grandfather

characters.description: A near-human Hegemony scientist whose eidetic memory may preserve the text of the destroyed book. She will reconstruct it only if Galina Turov authorizes the revival of her dead friend, whose data she has retained.
characters.name: Florimel

characters.description: A deceased enemy agent who was close to Florimel and previously killed both her and McGill. Florimel holds his preserved DNA and memories, and makes his revival the price of reproducing the destroyed book.
characters.name: Rash

characters.description: Legion Varus's senior primus and operational commander beneath Galina Turov. He briefs the legion's officers aboard their new transport as an unusually early deployment begins.
characters.name: Graves

characters.description: A legionnaire in McGill's Third Unit. She joins the unit as Legion Varus prepares for an early deployment with its destination still undisclosed.
characters.name: Kivi

characters.description: A Legion Varus veteran serving in McGill's Third Unit as the legion begins an early deployment whose purpose remains undisclosed.
characters.name: Harris

characters.description: An adjunct in Third Unit who temporarily commands it while McGill is absent. He is part of the established officer group preparing the unit for its new mission.
characters.name: Leeson

characters.description: A member of McGill's Third Unit who deploys with Legion Varus aboard its new transport.
characters.name: Carlos

characters.description: McGill's friend and a Legion Varus centurion preparing for the legion's new deployment.
characters.name: Manfred

characters.description: An experienced former centurion transferred from Legion Victrix into McGill's unit after refusing a Hegemony desk post. Visibly uneasy about joining Varus, she does not explain why Victrix removed her from combat duty.
characters.name: Former Victrix adjunct

characters.description: McGill's former partner, Etta's mother, and a native of Dust World. She confronts him over their daughter's dangerous experience there and fears Etta's continuing determination to enter legion service.
characters.name: Della

characters.description: A Third Unit specialist who openly questions McGill's training plan before a shipboard war game. His willingness to challenge the centurion marks him as an independently minded member of the unit.
characters.name: Cooper

characters.description: A senior noncommissioned weapons specialist in Third Unit. During the Green Deck exercise, he coordinates the plasma attack on an enemy tower and helps carry an overloaded weapon toward the breach.
characters.name: Sargon

characters.description: A Mogwa chief inspector who expects McGill to deliver the bioterminator text. Galina Turov identifies him as the recipient of McGill's concealed courier mission.
characters.name: Xlur

characters.description: A former Legion Varus officer now working for the Hegemony. He treats McGill as absent without leave and sends him through a gateway to Storm World.
characters.name: Winslade

characters.description: A Blood World sub-centurion who recognizes McGill's standing among his troops and escorts him to the Iron Eagles primus.
characters.name: Churn

characters.description: The hostile Blood World officer commanding the Iron Eagles position on Storm World. Although McGill recognizes him from an earlier campaign, the primus refuses to help him rejoin Legion Varus.
characters.name: Iron Eagles primus

characters.description: The officer leading Third Unit's vulnerable light platoon. She maintains a professional bearing when McGill returns from a long absence.
characters.name: Barton

characters.description: A veteran reassigned by McGill to provide experienced support for Barton's vulnerable light platoon.
characters.name: Mahler

characters.description: A Third Unit soldier preparing to transfer into bio-specialist work. She declines the opportunity to train as a stealth scout and is willing to leave Legion Varus if the new specialty does not suit her.
characters.name: Sarah

characters.description: Third Unit's leading technical specialist. During the first patrol on Storm World, she identifies the sudden growth of immense vegetation as evidence of Wur activity.
characters.name: Natasha

characters.description: A blue scupper who formally recognizes McGill as First Man after McGill defeats the natives' previous leader. He becomes McGill's deputy within the newly acquired scupper force.
characters.name: Second Man

characters.description: The former commander of Legion Germanica, now tribune of Fort Beta's Blood World legion. He is a prior opponent of McGill and an antagonistic but necessary ally as the surviving forces prepare for another Wur assault.
characters.name: Maurice Armel

characters.description: The former grand admiral of Battlefleet 921 and newly appointed Mogwa governor of the province. He arrives at Storm World to judge Earth's frontier performance and orders the human force to prove itself in the coming battle.
characters.name: Governor Sateekas

characters.description: A former adversary of McGill and Florimel who now operates Fort Beta's oversized revival machinery. He is capable of processing giant bodies and is currently Florimel's partner.
characters.name: Saurian revival technician

characters.description: The ruler of the underground scupper city. She is hosting a Rigelian negotiator, has authority over alliance terms, and agrees to arbitrate McGill's challenge under native custom.
characters.name: Native queen

characters.description: Rigel's representative in the scupper capital and a fighter McGill encountered during an earlier campaign. He seeks an alliance with the native population and accepts McGill's customary challenge before the queen.
characters.name: Squanto

characters.description: The named female Claver. Female clones are forbidden within the Claver network.
characters.name: Abigail

characters.description: A separate Claver who claims exile from the primary clone line. He says he created the female clone Abigail, is hunted by the other Clavers, and offers McGill a plan to change the battle.
characters.name: Renegade Claver

characters.description: The renegade clone who joins McGill's force and proposes destroying the final Wur nexus to remove the local Wur's command intelligence.
characters.name: Claver-X

description.text: The tenth Undying Mercenaries novel opens with James McGill covering for his daughter Etta after she took payment from Claver by handing him a substitute in place of a dangerous book, then fled to Dust World with the money - only to find that the real book, which he thought was safely hidden, has vanished as well. Chasing the truth to Dust World, where an outlawed process can secretly revive the dead, McGill recovers the real book from Etta just as a newly revived enemy destroys it and kills him in the same encounter. While his superiors search for a way to reconstruct its contents from a witness's memory, Legion Varus is called up for an early, unexplained deployment to Storm World to intervene against the plant-like Wur on behalf of a besieged frontier population.

recaps.ending: McGill destroys the final Wur nexus and dies inside it. Sarah performs an accelerated revival, and he learns that the disconnected Wur attacked both Fort Beta and their Rigelian allies. Sateekas judges the human army inferior in direct combat, but Squanto refuses to make Rigel the province's new enforcer. Earth therefore retains the position, and McGill uses the promised truce to return Squanto alive. Rigel withdraws and transmits Florimel's engram, enabling her revival. She confirms that she surrendered the genuine Mogwa-killing formula to Rigel. Legion Varus evacuates Storm World, while Maurice Armel's legion remains behind to rebuild with the scuppers. Two months later, Claver-X brings Etta home. Central and the primary Claver line are hunting him, but McGill hides their contact and kills two pursuing clones. Galina Turov resumes her relationship with McGill while warning that the Core Worlds are investigating Xlur's permadeath. The formula's spread, Claver-X's role, Florimel's plan to seek her partner's revival, and McGill's exposure remain open.
recaps.in_short: James McGill pursues Etta and a book containing a Mogwa-killing formula, survives illegal revivals, and kills Chief Inspector Xlur while hiding the formula's loss. Legion Varus deploys to Storm World against the Wur, where McGill gains command of the native scuppers. Rigel intervenes, and Governor Sateekas makes Earth's provincial status depend on the conflict. Maurice Armel betrays the garrison and helps Claver Prime trade Florimel to Rigel. A renegade Claver-X then guides McGill toward the final Wur nexus. McGill destroys it and dies, but Sarah revives him. The leaderless Wur attack both armies, and Rigel withdraws. Sateekas keeps Earth as local enforcer only because Squanto refuses the appointment. Florimel returns by transmitted engram and admits giving Rigel the genuine formula. Varus leaves, Armel remains to rebuild, and Etta later comes home with Claver-X while the formula, Xlur investigation, and clone conflict remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: James McGill serves as a centurion in Legion Varus under Tribune Galina Turov, with whom he also has a personal relationship. His daughter Etta wants a military life, while her parents remain divided over the dangers surrounding her. Claver is not a single ordinary adversary but part of a clone network whose bodies and memories complicate any attempt to stop him permanently. McGill has also dealt with Florimel, a near-human Hegemony scientist, and with the Mogwa officials who oversee Earth's place in Province 921. His history includes campaigns involving Blood World forces, the Wur, Rigel, and officers such as Maurice Armel and Sateekas. These relationships leave McGill caught between family obligations, legion command, and the demands of powers that can determine humanity's status.

Etta has left for Dust World after secretly selling Claver a false copy of a valuable book. Claver confronts McGill and demands the genuine volume, which contains a formula for a genetic poison lethal to the Mogwa. McGill discovers that the real book is missing, kills one Claver body, and uses its teleport equipment to follow Etta. Two worker clones attack him on Dust World and send him to his death. Etta's grandfather restores McGill through an illegal colonial revival process and warns that exposure would endanger them all. McGill then finds Etta, who returns the real book and explains that she feared its use as a mass weapon. The colony has revived one of the worker clones as a more capable Claver. It attacks McGill and Etta, destroying the book and mortally wounding McGill before Etta kills it. McGill dies again, and the physical text appears lost.

McGill returns through another irregular revival and reports to Galina Turov. Because Central has no copy of the destroyed book, he brings her to Florimel, whose eidetic memory can reproduce it. Florimel demands the revival of her dead friend in exchange. Before that bargain is resolved, Legion Varus deploys early aboard Leggett to Storm World, an oceanic frontier planet threatened by the plantlike Wur. A separate Blood World legion accompanies it. During a shipboard exercise designed to favor the non-revivable Blood World troops, McGill forces a breach and causes permanent losses on the opposing side. Galina and Graves execute him off the record, but the death also conceals a courier mission. Florimel's encrypted message was supposed to carry the bioterminator text to Chief Inspector Xlur. McGill reveals only after dying that he deleted the message without reading it. He is now committed to meeting Xlur without the data the Mogwa official expects.

McGill revives on Mogwa Prime, where Chief Inspector Xlur expects the missing formula. Xlur is an exiled official who hopes the information will restore his political position. McGill pretends that the nonexistent file requires his personal translation, using the delay to study his confinement. When Xlur moves to kill him, McGill reverses the attack and disintegrates the inspector. He then sends Galina a false confirmation of delivery, fabricates evidence that Xlur killed himself, and takes his own life so that he can be revived elsewhere. McGill returns off-grid on Earth after four months away and learns that Leggett has already departed. A former Varus officer sends him through a gateway to Storm World. He arrives inside an isolated Blood World fort during lethal tides and storms, but its hostile primus refuses to help him reach Varus and shoots him. McGill has reached the campaign, but only through another death and another concealed chain of events.

After repeated transfers and revivals, McGill rejoins Third Unit on Storm World and restores his command. Galina confirms that she concealed his Core Worlds mission and begins limited patrols against the Wur. McGill's first patrol encounters rapidly grown forest and pod walkers. The unit defeats the attack but loses equipment and personnel. Ordered to stop a scupper war party from cutting Wur trees, McGill instead faces a series of unexplained disappearances. He, Cooper, and Kivi fall into an underground transport network created by the native scuppers. Kivi dies while testing its gravity-shifting tubes, but McGill retains the information needed for her revival. Cooper and McGill learn to navigate the system and emerge far from their unit on a coastal beach. As a major storm and tide approach, hundreds of scuppers surround them at the cliff top. McGill sends the concealed Cooper away to report and remains alone to attempt contact with the native force.

A scupper leader challenges McGill's courage. McGill defeats and spares him, and the natives recognize McGill as their new First Man. He gains roughly seven hundred fighters and a deputy called Second Man. Galina allows the scuppers into Fort Alpha, but their earlier destruction of Wur trees has already drawn a large response. During the assault, McGill arms the natives and holds the eastern gate while other sections collapse. Wur acid troops and pod walkers overrun most of the fort, leaving the remaining defenders trapped in Gold Bunker. Second Man identifies a buried entrance to the native transport tubes. McGill persuades Galina to abandon the final bunker and leads the survivors underground as the Wur break in. Sixteen humans and a much larger scupper group use the network to reach Fort Beta. Its automated defenses kill Harris before McGill destroys the weapon and secures entry. Fort Alpha has fallen, but Galina, McGill, and their remaining organized force survive at the stronger Blood World position.

At Fort Beta, Galina and Tribune Maurice Armel form an uneasy alliance. A ship belonging to Governor Sateekas arrives to judge whether Earth remains capable of enforcing order on the frontier. Galina uses the gateway network to seek reinforcements. She later commands Leggett when three Rigelian transports attack. Leggett destroys one ship and escapes the missile response by entering warp, leaving the ground force isolated. Thousands of armored Rigelian troops land inside the fort while Wur forces gather outside. McGill discovers that captured Rigelian guns and extended human force blades can defeat their resistant armor, helping Varus repel the landing at severe cost. Florimel is present with Armel's near-human troops and is now partnered with a Saurian revival technician. Before the garrison can recover, the Wur attack Fort Beta. Their pod walkers climb over wounded members of their own force to reach the battlements. By the end of the assault's opening phase, the wall defense has failed and the defenders must prepare for close combat inside the fort.

Armel commits his giant troops and personally leads a counterattack that defeats the Wur breach, though the giants suffer irreplaceable losses and Kivi is trampled. Graves then sends McGill to reconnect with the scuppers. McGill reaches their vast underground city and finds a Rigelian representative negotiating with the native queen. He challenges the Rigelian under local custom, wins the unarmed contest, and gains command of the native armies. Governor Sateekas nevertheless refuses to declare Earth victorious while Rigel and the Wur remain active. McGill returns to Fort Beta with about three thousand native volunteers and begins turning them into a disciplined force. Natasha then shows him restricted intelligence indicating that Rigelian and Wur troops are occupying the same area without fighting. Armel's guards arrest them, and Natasha is killed during the struggle. McGill reports the apparent alliance to Armel and Graves. To keep their attention and gain leverage, he falsely claims that he may have a way to communicate with the Wur.

Maurice Armel reveals that he knows about the bioterminator book and wants McGill to obtain another copy for a buyer. Convinced that the Rigel-Wur alliance has doomed the campaign, he plans to evacuate the officers and abandon the garrison. When Graves objects, Armel shoots him. Claver Prime arrives under a deal with Armel, takes McGill captive, and abducts Florimel after killing her Saurian partner. He sells Florimel to Rigel for the formula in her memory and delivers McGill to Sateekas as cover for the trade. McGill attacks Claver and tries to redirect blame for Xlur's death, but Sateekas privately reveals that he already knows McGill killed the inspector. The governor regards that death as useful. He also explains that an Imperial succession crisis has nearly destroyed his former fleet. Rigel has been offered Earth's place as provincial enforcer, and humanity will be expunged if its army loses the approaching battle. McGill returns to warn the garrison and is immediately imprisoned by Armel's troops.

As Rigelian and Wur forces march together against Fort Beta, Cooper frees McGill from the brig. McGill warns Armel, then encounters a Claver who is separate from the Prime held by Sateekas. This renegade, later called Claver-X, says he created the forbidden female clone Abigail and was exiled by the primary line. He proposes destroying the final Wur nexus, the command intelligence coordinating the planet's plant forces. McGill accepts and leads Third Unit, scuppers, and Claver-X through the mountains while the main armies assault the fort. Rigelian troops inflict heavy losses along the route, and lethal tides kill more of the expedition. McGill eventually sends the heavies back and reaches the nexus on an isolated plateau. With no explosives, he attacks it using a captured shotgun and force blades. Floodwater cuts off his escape, but he penetrates the nexus and destroys it after a drone receives his final data. McGill dies inside the structure, leaving the Wur without centralized direction.

Sarah revives McGill through an accelerated procedure. Although Fort Beta is devastated, the destruction of the nexus has driven the Wur out of control, and they attack both the defenders and their Rigelian allies. Sateekas rules that Earth was inferior in direct battle and offers its enforcer role to Rigel. Squanto refuses Imperial service, so Sateekas retains Earth instead. McGill invokes the governor's safe-passage promise to save Squanto from execution. Rigel withdraws and sends Florimel's mental engram, allowing Sarah to revive her. Florimel confirms that she gave Rigel the genuine Mogwa-killing formula. Varus evacuates, while Armel's legion remains on Storm World to rebuild with the scuppers. Two months later, Claver-X returns Etta safely to Earth. McGill kills two worker clones pursuing him and conceals the encounter from Galina. She warns that Central and the primary Claver line are hunting Claver-X, while the Core Worlds are investigating Xlur's permadeath. Etta is home and Earth retains its status, but the formula, the clone conflict, and McGill's possible exposure remain unresolved.
